api_key.description: Hyperping API key (starts with `sk_`). Can also be set via `HYPERPING_API_KEY` environment variable.

base_url.description: Hyperping API base URL. Defaults to `https://api.hyperping.io`.

mcp_url.description: Hyperping MCP server URL. Defaults to `https://api.hyperping.io/v1/mcp`.

block.description: The Hyperping provider allows you to manage Hyperping monitors, incidents, and maintenance windows.

cron.description: Cron expression defining the schedule (e.g., `0 0 * * *`). Mutually exclusive with `period_value`/`period_type`.

escalation_policy.description: UUID of the escalation policy to link to this healthcheck.

grace_period_value.description: Numeric value for the grace period buffer before alerting. For example, set `grace_period_value = 5` with `grace_period_type = "minutes"` to allow a 5-minute window.

id.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the healthcheck.

is_down.description: Whether the healthcheck is currently in a failure state (read-only).

is_paused.description: Whether the healthcheck is paused. Defaults to `false`.

last_ping.description: Timestamp of the last ping received in ISO 8601 format (read-only).

period_value.description: Numeric value for the expected interval. Mutually exclusive with `cron`/`tz`.

ping_url.description: The auto-generated ping URL. Your cron job pings this URL to prove it ran.

timezone.description: Timezone for the cron expression (e.g., `America/New_York`). Required when `cron` is set.

block.description: Manages a Hyperping healthcheck for cron job monitoring (dead man's switch).

affected_components.description: List of monitor UUIDs representing components affected by this incident. Displayed on the associated status pages.

date.description: The date of the incident in ISO 8601 format (read-only).

id.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the incident.

status_pages.description: List of status page UUIDs to display this incident on. Required.

text.description: The description text of the incident (English).

type.description: The type of incident. Valid values: `outage`, `incident`. Defaults to `incident`.

block.description: Manages a Hyperping incident for status page updates.

date.description: The date of the update in ISO 8601 format. If not provided, the current time is used.

id.description: The unique identifier of the update (format: incident_id/update_id).

incident_id.description: The UUID of the incident to add the update to.

text.description: The text content of the update (English).

type.description: The type of update. Valid values: `investigating`, `identified`, `update`, `monitoring`, `resolved`.

block.description: Manages an update to a Hyperping incident. Use this to add status updates to an incident timeline.

end_date.description: The scheduled end time in ISO 8601 format (e.g., `2026-01-20T04:00:00.000Z`).

id.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the maintenance window.

monitors.description: List of monitor UUIDs affected by this maintenance window.

name.description: The internal name of the maintenance window.

notification_minutes.description: Number of minutes before the maintenance to notify subscribers. Defaults to `60`. Only used when notification_option is `scheduled`. Must be at least 1.

notification_option.description: When to notify subscribers. Valid values: `none`, `scheduled`, `immediate`. Defaults to `none` (no notification).

start_date.description: The scheduled start time in ISO 8601 format (e.g., `2026-01-20T02:00:00.000Z`).

status_pages.description: List of status page UUIDs to display this maintenance on.

text.description: The description text of the maintenance (English).

title.description: The public title of the maintenance window (English).

block.description: Manages a Hyperping maintenance window for scheduled downtime.

alerts_wait.description: Minutes to wait before sending alerts after an outage is detected. Must be one of: `-1` (disabled), `0`, `1`, `2`, `3`, `5`, `10`, `30`, `60`.

dns_expected_answer.description: Expected DNS answer to validate against. Only valid when protocol is `dns`. Monitor fails if the resolved value does not contain this string.

dns_nameserver.description: Nameserver to query against (e.g., `8.8.8.8`). Only valid when protocol is `dns`. Leave empty to use default resolvers.

dns_record_type.description: DNS record type to check. Only valid when protocol is `dns`. Valid values: `A`, `AAAA`, `CNAME`, `MX`, `NS`, `TXT`, `SOA`, `SRV`, `CAA`, `PTR`. Defaults to `A` (set by the API if omitted).

escalation_policy.description: UUID of the escalation policy to link to this monitor.

escalation_policy_name.description: Human-readable name of the assigned escalation policy.

expected_status_code.description: Expected HTTP status code pattern. Use a specific code like `200`, a wildcard like `2xx` (200-299), or a range like `1xx-3xx` (100-399). Defaults to `2xx`.

follow_redirects.description: Whether to follow HTTP redirects. Only applies to `http` protocol monitors. Defaults to `true`.

http_method.description: HTTP method to use. Only valid when protocol is `http`. Valid values: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`. Defaults to `GET`.

id.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the monitor.

is_down.description: Whether the monitor is currently reporting as down.

name.description: The display name of the monitor. Must be 1-255 characters.

paused.description: Whether the monitor is paused. Defaults to `false`.

port.description: TCP port number (1-65535). Required when protocol is `port`. Examples: `443` (HTTPS), `5432` (PostgreSQL), `6379` (Redis).

project_uuid.description: UUID of the Hyperping project this monitor belongs to.

protocol.description: The protocol type. Valid values: `http`, `port`, `icmp`, `dns`. Defaults to `http`.

regions.description: List of monitoring regions. Use the `hyperping_monitoring_locations` data source to discover available locations.

request_body.description: HTTP request body. Only valid when protocol is `http` and http_method is `POST`, `PUT`, or `PATCH`.

name.description: The header name. Must be a valid HTTP token (RFC 7230). Reserved headers that control HTTP framing or routing are not allowed: `Host`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Content-Length`, `Connection`, `Upgrade`, `TE`, `Trailer`, `Expect`.

value.description: The header value. Marked sensitive: masked in plan output and Terraform CLI display. Values are still stored in state, so credentials require a secure state backend.

request_headers.description: Custom HTTP headers to send with the request. Only valid when protocol is `http`. `Authorization` and `Cookie` are allowed for probing endpoints behind authentication; because values may contain credentials, the `value` field is marked sensitive and is persisted to Terraform state. Use a secure state backend if you put secrets here.

required_keyword.description: A keyword that must appear in the HTTP response body for the check to pass. Only valid when protocol is `http`.

ssl_expiration.description: Days until the SSL certificate expires.

url.description: The URL to monitor. For HTTP/ICMP/port protocols, must include scheme (e.g., `https://api.example.com/health`). For DNS protocol, use a bare domain (e.g., `example.com`).

The value is accepted by Terraform but will not appear on the rendered status page. Use descriptions on top-level (non-group) services instead.

Status pages provide a public or private view of your service health, allowing you to communicate incidents and maintenance to your users.

Manages a subscriber for a Hyperping status page.

Subscribers receive notifications about incidents and maintenance. Supported types: email, sms, teams. Note: Slack subscribers must be added via OAuth flow and cannot be managed via API.

All fields are immutable - any change will recreate the subscriber.
